#  Title:MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
Authors:[Jingwei Song](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Song,+J), [Zhisheng Chen](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Chen,+Z), [Bingfan Zeng](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Zeng,+B), [Jing Tang](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Tang,+J), [Yubo Hou](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Hou,+Y), [Jinhao Jing](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Jing,+J), [Zhengwei Xie](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Xie,+Z), [Linfeng Zhang](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Zhang,+L)
View a PDF of the paper titled MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents, by Jingwei Song and 7 other authors
[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13829v1) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.13829v1)
> Abstract:A central challenge in embodied recursive self-improvement is enabling agents to convert interaction history into capabilities that persist beyond one world and transfer to later tasks. A saved memory or successful final action does not by itself establish that a reusable capability was acquired; evaluation must separate capability change from carried-over resources, unequal source exposure, and early execution failures. We construct MC-EvoBench as a controlled Minecraft benchmark with a fixed catalog of 19 registered evolution chains, including 12 primary evaluation chains and seven calibration or probe chains, together with three graph-aligned paired probe families for transfer. The benchmark represents each task as a task-state graph, defines stage-level environment verifiers, assigns matched source and target roles, resets the target world, and permits only a declared agent artifact to cross the source-target boundary. For each probe, no-prior, related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions are evaluated under matched environment-step budgets and five seeds; we report TSR, WGP, and VMP and retain provenance records. The benchmark reveals a consistent direct-capability gap between controller and planner-backed variants, while related experience yields no stable transfer: it does not improve either tool probe, its small wood-species gain hinges on one seed, and all intervals include zero. Stage audits further show that early wood-collection and crafting bottlenecks often leave later capabilities unobserved. MC-EvoBench thus offers a controlled testbed for durable, transferable embodied capabilities. Code and data are available at [this https URL](https://github.com/xzw-ustc/mc-bench-open-source)

|  Hi, maybe this strong take deserves a bit of context of why we want to go further than the previous "Human in the loop" policy
  * AI use from external contributors puts a massive and unbearable pressure on the shoulders of our maintainers, who already had a though job before the era of LLM's
  * AI stream is a lot higher than what human review can take seriously, leading to either a longer list of un-reviewed PR's or not fully reviewed code and quality issues. Both thing we don't want in the project.
  * Free software communities are build on human network . QGIS is trusted by organisations because they know they can contribute back, they can hire contributors for support, training and feature. As a community project, this is something we really want to protect, and keep having enough bandwith to be welcoming to human contributions.
So, for this reason, a huge +1 for me.  
Thanks a lot for opening the QEP, given the pressure context you are in [@nyalldawson](https://github.com/nyalldawson) , much appreciated. I'd like to open another topic about the usage of LLM for review, auditing and security purposes, but I think this is a very separate thread, and we'll open discussions at the user conference before any formal discussions. Things are moving so fast, let's first tackle this QEP.  |
